notes.text: Claim: with LockRecursionPolicy.SupportsRecursion, calling EnterWriteLock while holding a plain read lock still throws LockRecursionException (upgrade from read mode is never allowed). The ReaderWriterLockSlim docs state that read-to-write upgrade is not permitted because it is prone to deadlocks; please confirm that the exception type is LockRecursionException in both policies.

Expected run: the snippet throws an unhandled System.Threading.LockRecursionException at line 19 on the first Get call before anything is printed; fixedSource prints "10" twice (key "a" has length 1, times 10). Please confirm with run-snippets.

bugLineSets accepts [12, 19], [12] and [19]: the root cause is EnterReadLock on line 12, and the throwing call is EnterWriteLock on line 19. The alternative fix (release the read lock before taking the write lock) changes the code around line 19, which is why line 19 alone is also accepted. The owner may want to narrow this.
Claim: only one thread can be in upgradeable read mode at a time, while it can coexist with ordinary readers. This is stated in the ReaderWriterLockSlim docs.
